$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §2 and docs/04-ARCHITECTURE.md §3. The canonical form of this object, under c14n v1, is what profile_sha256 hashes; the example below is the real v0 profile and its real digest, emitted by crates/engine-core and pinned in its tests.
title: Engine profile (DRAFT)
description: Every knob that can change output. Anything that can change a byte of output belongs here or is a bug. Host-varying data (paths, timings, thread counts, machine identity) is deliberately absent: including it would make every machine produce a different fingerprint for identical work.

parser_version.description: The engine build this profile describes. A new build is a new profile by design.

backend.description: Object/xref backend identity, so adopting or upgrading it is fingerprint-visible.

classify_sample_pages.description: How many pages classification samples before it stops. Default 8. Its boundedness is the point: cost must not scale with total page count.

reading_order_rule.description: Version id of the reading-order rule in force. Versioned because the rule is part of identity: when a stable multi-column rule lands it gets a new id here rather than silently replacing this one.

cmap_data_version.description: Identity of the vendored character-decoding data. Names what is actually vendored rather than what was planned: at M3 that is the PDF 32000-1 Annex D encoding tables, not the Adobe predefined CJK CMaps, whose absence is a declared limitation.

xref_repair.description: Whether the one bounded cross-reference repair runs (v0.1). On the profile because it decides which documents produce an artifact at all.

verifier.description: Which verifier this run is bound to (v0.1). `not_pinned` is a declared state, not a missing field: the engine does not verify, it invokes a verifier, and a run that consulted none says so.

form_annotation_rule.description: Version id of the forms-and-annotations rule in force (v1-S4). Decides which form-field and annotation nodes exist: which flag bits are named, how a fully-qualified field name is built, and the fact that a widget's rendering is never read as page text. Named for what it does rather than the structure it reads, because engine-core carries no format concept.

struct_tree_rule.description: Version id of the structure-tree rule in force (v1-S3). Decides which runs come out carrying a role path: the recognised structure types, the /RoleMap handling, the /K depth bound, and the fact that the (page, mcid) join is exact equality rather than anything looser.

table_detection.description: The table-detection rules in force. An object rather than a string since v1-S2: with two rules running, a single id could not say whether a run looked for unruled tables and found none or never looked, and those are different documents to a consumer. Every table on the wire also names the rule that produced it.

ruled.description: Version id of the rule that reconstructs grids from rectangles the document painted. `ruled-rects-v1`.

unruled.description: Version id of the rule that infers grids from text alignment. `unruled-align-v1`. A table it produced was inferred by this engine, not drawn by the author — which is why the two ids are separate.

capabilities.title: What this profile claims it can do
capabilities.description: L1's achievement condition names capability declarations explicitly, so an artifact without them has not reached 'extracted' regardless of how good its text is. The first three mirror ethos.grounding.v1's required capabilities object exactly.
capabilities.$comment: Two rules bind this object in both directions, and both are enforced by tests rather than by review. No `true` without a named proof test: crates/engine-pdf/tests/capabilities.rs maps each true field to a test function and fails the build when the named test does not exist. No `false` without a declared limitation: Capabilities::declared_limitations() derives one per false field, exhaustively, so a consumer never infers a gap from silence.

char_offsets.$comment: FALSE in v0, and it was true in the M1 sketch. v0 emits runs with native locators and no element/span hierarchy, so there is nothing for an offset to index into. It flips at M5 with DocumentRepresentation v0 — and with a test. Narrowing a declaration when the evidence does not support it is the mechanism working, not a regression.

tables.$comment: true since v1-S1 (ruled), widened at v1-S2 (unruled)

measured_ink_boxes.$comment: true in v0 — proof: measured_ink_boxes_are_measured_and_absence_stays_typed, which asserts both halves (a measured box exists, and unusable metrics still yield typed absence rather than a fallback)

multi_column_reading_order.$comment: false in v0 — single-column only, and the limitation is declared on every artifact and pinned by the synthetic/two-columns golden

structural_locators.$comment: FALSE in v0. An mcid IS captured where a page's content stream supplies one via BDC, and never invented where it does not — but the tagged-structure tree is not read, so there is no role path and an absent mcid is not evidence the document is untagged. Claiming the capability on the strength of the partial half would promise an address consumers could not rely on.

page_budget.title: How many pages a run may process before it stops
page_budget.$comment: A DECLARED STATE, not an absent field: {"mode":"unlimited"} says the budget was considered and found unbounded, where an omitted optional would leave a reader unable to tell 'unbounded' from 'this build has no such knob' — and would deserialize to a default that silently re-hashes as though it had been there. A page count is the knob because it is the bound that actually governs peak cost in a page-at-a-time reader. Setting it changes profile_sha256, so a budgeted run is correctly non-comparable with an unbudgeted one.

oneOf.description: No page bound. The v0 default.

pages.$comment: Zero is legal and means 'process none'. It is the only budget that can bite on a one-page document, which is what failure/memory-limit-simulated needs: that fixture is byte-identical to synthetic/simple-text, so its name means the limit is simulated BY CONFIGURATION, not that the PDF is large.

oneOf.description: Process at most this many pages; the rest are quarantined and declared, and the run's terminal state is partial.
